subject: Post-call: Vendor bake-off recap & agreed next steps
messages:
From: Karthik Iyer <karthik.iyer@redwood.com>
To: Sara Humphrey <sara.humphrey@acme-retail.com>, Mike Turner <mike.turner@acme-retail.com>
Cc: Laura Bennett <laura.bennett@redwood.com>, Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.com>, Rachel Kim <rachel.kim@redwood.com>
Date: Fri, 10 Apr 2026 16:02:00 -0700
Subject: Post-call: Vendor bake-off recap & agreed next steps

Hi Sara / Mike — thanks again for the time today. Quick recap from our conversation and the concrete next steps so we have alignment before the evaluation week.

Summary of pain & goals (what you emphasized)
- High variability in traffic (holiday spikes) — need predictable p95 latency under burst.
- Current infra cost with per-token provider is unpredictable; target is ~30% reduction in unit cost for chat features.
- Data residency & auditability: logs and key management must meet internal controls (no cross-region data without consent).
- Need a plan that doesn’t require a full in-house rebuild; preference for an opinionated serving runtime + integration guides.

Decision criteria you listed
1) Latency: p95 < 200ms for 512-token conversational flows
2) Cost: demonstrable unit economics at 1M tokens/day scale
3) Security: VPC option + KMS integration + audit logs
4) Model quality: parity with current SOTA baseline (human evals will be part of the bake-off)
5) Operations: rollouts, fallbacks, and obvious rollback plan for model changes

Competitive bake-off notes
- We discussed running Redwood alongside AtlasAI and the Big Cloud Provider as a three-way test.
- Agreed test vectors: 1) synthetic latency benchmark (steady + spike), 2) 48-hour production-shaped replay (anonymized), 3) two A/B qualitative evals on customer-facing prompts.

Open questions / clarifications we captured from today
- AtlasAI indicated they might not support prefix/KV caching in their managed offering — we flagged this as relevant to latency/cost.
- Procurement: ACME needs an initial SOW + standard security questionnaire (SOC attestation). Mike to confirm timelines for security review.

Next steps (owner / ETA)
- Karthik: Send scorecard template + Redwood test checklist (attached) — today (done).
- Acme (Sara): Confirm procurement window and add required security artifacts — by EOD Mon 2026-04-13.
- Redwood (Marissa): Run a short latency pilot on your staging traffic sample (we'll ask for the replay file) — target: start 2026-04-15.
- All: 1-week bake-off, follow-up decision review meeting week of 2026-04-22.

Attachments: redwood-bakeoff-scorecard.xlsx (scorecard + test definitions), mutual-action-plan.pdf (timeline + roles).

If I missed anything, please flag — otherwise I’ll schedule the kickoff and send the Drive link for test artifacts.

Thanks,
Karthik
--

Subject: Re: Post-call: Vendor bake-off recap & agreed next steps

Thanks Karthik — helpful summary. A couple quick clarifications from procurement/security: 

- Can you confirm which SOC reports Redwood can provide for an evaluation? (SOC 2 Type II + date range)
- We will need a sample KMS integration guide and confirmation about region-locking for logs.
- Timeline: procurement can turn around an initial SOW in ~5 business days after we receive the standard security package.

Mike and I are comfortable with the proposed test vectors — please include the exact schema for the replay file so our infra team can anonymize accordingly.

Also: on cost targets — the 30% number is a rough target, not a hard requirement. If Redwood can show predictable ops and a path to cost parity with clear levers (batching/quantization), that will be compelling.

Sara

Head of AI Platforms, Acme Retail

Sara — thanks, noted. Short answers now and I’ll attach the artifacts again: 

- SOC: Redwood can provide SOC 2 Type II report (last audit March 2026) and a summary of controls. I’ve attached the standard security pack and KMS integration guide.
- Region-locking: we support VPC private deployment and can ensure logs remain in your chosen region for the pilot; the private option takes slightly longer to provision (we included timelines in the MAP).
- Replay schema: attached in the Drive link and included inside the scorecard under the "Test Data" tab. We recommended a 10k-100k message sample for the 48-hour replay (anonymized).

Pilot/practical notes:
- Marissa will run the latency pilot with your replay file. We’ll spin up a test harness with two model configs: a quantized Llama-2 variant and our recommended parity model. AtlasAI will run the same harness for parity.
- We propose a short smoke test (5k messages) day 1 to validate connectivity, then a 48-hour run day 2–3. Expect a preliminary latency + cost report within 48 hours after the run.

Next step for us: I’ll create the calendar invite for the 2026-04-15 kickoff and upload the test harness docs to Drive. 

Karthik

Subject: Internal: Prep notes for ACME bake-off (prep before kickoff)

Karthik / team — quick internal checklist before we start the pilot: 

- Marissa: validate that our quantized runtime has the expected p95 improvement on the 512-token baseline (use current benchmark harness). Flag any model mismatch early.
- Rachel: prep the audit log export sample and KMS onboarding checklist for Acme’s security team.
- Karthik: confirm the exact SLAs we’ll propose for the pilot period (we punt enterprise SLA sign-off until after evaluation).

Competitive angle: AtlasAI may try to undercut on list price but they lack prefix caching; call that out explicitly in the scorecard under latency drivers.

I’ll join the kickoff and take notes on the qualitative eval session. Keep comms tight — we want to hit the 48-hour turnaround for the report.

Laura
